rationale: Evidence from a prenatal diagnostic cohort specifically evaluating isolated fetal horseshoe kidney (HSK) demonstrates that pathogenic PSMD12 variants occur at a low frequency. In the study by Yu et al. (2026), 95 fetuses presented with isolated HSK on prenatal ultrasound and were evaluated via CMA, with 45 negative cases proceeding to trio exome sequencing. Exactly one fetus harbored a disease-causing variant in PSMD12 (c.796-1G > A), accounting for 1/45 (2.2%) of exome-sequenced cases and 1/95 (1.05%) of all isolated HSK cases, both falling within the hypothesized '<5%' range. Furthermore, horseshoe kidney is a known manifestation in syndromic PSMD12-related disorders (Stankiewicz-Isidor syndrome), as documented by Küry et al. (2017). No contradicting cohorts or studies refuting this frequency were identified.

evidence.text: In a cohort of 95 fetuses with isolated horseshoe kidney diagnosed on second-trimester ultrasound, 45 CMA-negative cases underwent trio exome sequencing. Two monogenic disease-causing variants were identified: c.796-1G > A in PSMD12 and c.11707 C > T in KMT2D, demonstrating a PSMD12 diagnostic yield of 2.2% among exome-sequenced isolated HSK cases (1/45) and 1.05% overall (1/95).

source.title: Clinically Significant Genetic Results in Fetuses With Isolated Horseshoe Kidney
source.quote: Among the cases that yielded negative results from CMA, 45 proceeded to trio ES. Notably, two disease-causing variants, c.796-1G > A in PSMD12 and c.11707 C > T (p.Gln3903*) in KMT2D, were detected in each case.

evidence.text: Renal malformations including horseshoe kidney represent an established phenotypic component of de novo PSMD12 disruption causing Stankiewicz-Isidor syndrome.

source.title: De novo disruption of the proteasome regulatory subunit PSMD12 causes a syndromic neurodevelopmental disorder

new_directions.question_text: What proportion of fetuses with prenatal 'isolated' horseshoe kidney harboring PSMD12 variants exhibit subtle or uncharacterized extra-renal dysmorphology upon detailed postmortem or postnatal evaluation?
new_directions.rationale: Prenatal ultrasound may miss subtle craniofacial dysmorphism or minor structural abnormalities, making it essential to evaluate whether PSMD12 presentations are truly isolated CAKUT or early undetected manifestations of syndromic Stankiewicz-Isidor syndrome.

new_directions.question_text: What is the yield of PSMD12 sequencing in larger multicenter cohorts of isolated CAKUT categorized by structural subtype (e.g., horseshoe kidney vs. renal agenesis vs. MCDK)?
new_directions.rationale: Validating the 1-2% prevalence of PSMD12 variants across international multicenter CAKUT cohorts will determine standard inclusion criteria for prenatal gene sequencing panels.
